prompt: Build a ShoppingCart composed of a list of the provided CartItem records: add stores an item, itemCount sums all quantities, and total sums price times quantity per line (tests round to 2 decimals).
explanation: The cart is composed of small immutable data carriers: a record declares its fields once and Java generates the constructor and the name(), price(), qty() accessors automatically. itemCount and total are both accumulator loops over the composed list, reading record components instead of raw fields. Because doubles like 1.99 are not exactly representable in binary, the tests round to two decimals -- a common pattern when asserting on floating-point money.
hints: add just wraps the three arguments: items.add(new CartItem(name, price, qty));
Record components are read via methods: item.qty(), not item.qty -- sum those in a loop for itemCount.
For total, accumulate item.price() * item.qty() into a double starting at 0.0.
